title: Camunda closed the audit gap in 8.9 with a User Operations Audit Log
content:
The Orchestration Cluster API gained a user-task audit-log search marked *"Added in 8.9"*, and Camunda's own roadmap frames the pre-8.9 state as exactly the gap in question: organisations lacked a unified trail recording who did what, when, and to which entities. Release 8.9.16 shipped on 2026-08-14; the audit-log follow-up epic closed on 2026-03-10.

Retention ships disabled (`retention.enabled: false`, 30-day minimum age when switched on), which is a genuinely better default than most tools in this class.

The residual technical differences are real but too subtle to carry an argument: the log is documented as "Eventually Consistent" rather than transactionally coupled to the decision, and records live in ordinary mutable Elasticsearch indices with no hash chain. A demo asserting that Camunda cannot say who decided something would be factually wrong against 8.9 and corrected in the room.
description: The 8.9 release adds a queryable cross-domain log of who did what to which entity across process, identity and user-task domains, with retention disabled by default.
